Answers up-front to a couple of quick questions from the call (details below / will cover live):
- Chat vs completions: for structured tool-calling and reliable function outputs we recommend the chat endpoint with function-calling; completions are fine for freeform generation where you don't need structured JSON back.
- Streaming: set stream=true for delta token stream; you still need to parse partial JSON safely (we include examples in rsp-schema-examples.json).
- Tokenization / max_tokens: we included guidance in the tokenization cheatsheet  note that max_tokens is total model tokens; we recommend limiting assistant output with "max_output_tokens" in your wrapper to account for prompt + history.

David / Neha  forwarding Alex's questions. Quick internal notes below (we'll refine before the client session):

> 1) Chat vs completions: our engineer asked whether using chat for everything (including long-form docs summarization) has any cost/perf trade-offs compared to completions. Should we treat them differently in routing?

- Suggestion: Recommend chat for anything needing structured output or tool-calling (function-calling). For long-form summarization, completions can be slightly cheaper if you don't need function features, but difference is model-dependent. Provide both options in the playbook and recommend default routing policy: chat for interactive / assistant workflows, completions for batch summarization pipelines.

> 2) Streaming semantics: we want to stream partial results into our UI (token-by-token), but also reliably surface structured function outputs (e.g., a JSON action payload). Is there a recommended pattern to avoid broken JSON mid-stream?

- Suggestion: Use streaming for UI deltas and provide a separate finalization step: either 1) wait for a final non-streamed response to validate/emit the JSON payload, or 2) stream with explicit chunk framing and a final "__end_of_json__" sentinel. We have examples in rsp-schema-examples.json showing both patterns.

> 3) Embeddings / rerankers (20k docs): batching guidance? recommended embedding model?

- Suggestion: Use Redwood's recommended embedding model for semantic search (see guide). Batch size ~512 docs for throughput on GPU-backed ingestion, smaller batches for CPU. For reranking, compute dense embeddings and use approximate k-NN + a lightweight cross-encoder for top-k re-ranking if latency permits.

> 4) Auth: hosted API keys vs mTLS?

- Suggestion: For standard hosted usage, API keys + RBAC + audit logs suffice; for regulated customers wanting private network, offer private deployment with mTLS and KMS/HSM integration. We should pull in Security for any SOC2-specific asks.

I'll draft short canned answers we can paste into the call and add links to our playbook and code samples. Also  HubSpot record is 6221 (GAM-2026-042)  adding to the deal note after the session.

Marissa

Alex / Samira 

Thanks  Wed 9/16 10:00 PT works great; invite sent. Per your questions above, consolidated answers for the session (short version):

1) Chat vs Completions
- Use chat endpoints for interactive assistants and structured function-calling. The chat API includes first-class function-calling semantics which reduce parsing/validation work on your side.
- Use completions for batch, single-shot generation tasks where you don't need tooling/function features. Completions can be slightly more cost-effective for very large batch jobs, but test both for your workload.

2) Streaming + structured JSON
- Pattern A (recommended): stream token deltas for UI. In parallel, request a non-streamed finalization call (same prompt) that returns a validated JSON payload for downstream tooling.
- Pattern B: stream and include explicit framing (sentinel tokens / chunk metadata) and a final chunk containing the full JSON. Our examples (rsp-schema-examples.json) show both.

3) Tokenization / max_tokens / stop
- "max_tokens" is model-level limit (prompt + completion). We usually recommend you reserve headroom for the assistant output (use server-side wrapper param "max_output_tokens" = model_max - prompt_estimate).
- Stop sequences behave better with completions; with chat/function-calling, prefer explicit function return or structured outputs rather than stop-based trimming. See tokenization-cheatsheet.pdf for examples.

4) Embeddings / rerankers (20k docs)
- Start with our default embedding model (high-quality 1536-dim), batch ingestion (512) for GPU ingestion; use ANN for retrieval then a small cross-encoder for top-10 re-ranking if accuracy matters.

5) Auth / Private vs Hosted
- Hosted: API keys, RBAC, and audit logs. Private: VPC + mTLS + KMS integration; requires network prep (firewall rules, cert exchange). We'll loop in Security if they want SOC2-specific evidence.

Links / attachments included again: redwood-sdk-integration-guide.pdf (quickstart), rsp-schema-examples.json (function-calling + streaming patterns), tokenization-cheatsheet.pdf.

Please send one sample doc (or small bucket) for embeddings prior to the call if you want us to run a quick ingestion demo.
